newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Most Singapore shares up at open, SIA hits new low.
newsitem.headline: Most Singapore shares up at open, SIA hits new low.

text.p: The Singapore stock market was generally firmer in early trade on Thursday, continuing a bout of bargain-hunting for undervalued blue chips, dealers said.

But shares in national carrier Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA) fell to their lowest point for almost a year on selling by overseas funds in reaction to a poor set of half-year financial results released earlier in the week.
By 0145 GMT, the unweighted Straits Times Industrials Index was up 3.80 points at 2087.82.
SIA's foreign share tranche was down 20 cents at Singapore $12.40. Its local tranche was down five cents at S$7.40.
The latest fall comes after the publication of fairly gloomy comments by SIA's chief executive Cheong Choong Kong in a Reuters interview on Wednesday.

Cheong said the strength of the Singapore dollar and the weakness of the Japanese yen and the German mark were all hitting the company's performance. High jet fuel prices and a weak cargo market were also both negative factors, he said.
Top of the gainers on Thursday morning was drinks firm Fraser & Neave, which has been tipped as a buy by several local brokerages in recent weeks. It was up 20 cents at S$14.30.
